answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. The nectar is the held bond, the quartz the tenure multiplier, and the jetty the convex curve they ride; the nectar can be split but the quartz does not divide, and the jetty punishes the split. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
